fields.current_value: Would regulate large electric load customers of at least 50 MW, require co-located electric supplier licensing, require new large-load tariffs, require 100 percent load coverage plus reserve margin from new generation subject to waivers, and require financial guarantees to protect other ratepayers.
fields.primary_proposed_value: Would regulate large electric load customers with peak demand of at least 50 MW, license co-located suppliers, and require large-load tariffs and financial protections. Co-located suppliers would cover anticipated load plus reserve with qualifying new generation or incremental capacity, subject to waiver; tariff customers have separate generation requirements and waiver provisions.
fields.recommended_value: Would regulate customers with peak demand of at least 50 MW and license co-located suppliers. A co-located supplier would cover anticipated load plus reserve from generation entering service on or after July 1, 2026, or an adequate incremental increase to existing nameplate capacity, subject to a ratepayer and planning-based waiver. Proposed tariffs for later-interconnecting customers would separately require new generation that had not cleared a capacity auction, with a demand-flexibility waiver for customers not served by co-located suppliers, and financial protections for other ratepayers.
fields.rationale: Modified primary recommendation to identify the different generation and waiver conditions and scope of the tariff.
